title: AdvSim: Generating Safety-Critical Scenarios for Self-Driving Vehicles

control_signal.value: An adversarial objective chosen by the designer (hybrid of imitation, collision and comfort/safety cost terms; a subset such as collisions only can be used), applied to a black-box autonomy system under test.

control_mechanism.value: Black-box search (Bayesian optimization best) over a low-dimensional perturbation of actor kinematic-bicycle trajectories, projected onto a collision-free feasible set; LiDAR is re-simulated for each perturbed scene.

base_model.value: Not a learned generator: perturbs real logs with a high-fidelity LiDAR simulator; tested systems are IL, PLT, NMP and P3 autonomy stacks.

datasets.value: UrbanScenarios: 5,000 driving logs of 25 s from North American cities; curated to 3953 train and 409 val 6-second scenarios.

metrics.value: Collision rate (up to 3 or 5 s), L2 distance to human trajectory, jerk, lateral acceleration, detection AP at IoU 0.7, prediction L2 error, occupancy F1.

controllability_evidence.value: Generated scenarios give an average collision rate of 32.8 %, over 200 % more than the original set; for P3 collisions rise from 8.5 % to 32.0 %. Same-system targeting transfers best (Table 4 diagonal).

notes: Adversarial perturbation framework, not a generative traffic model; control is optimization of a cost, not user conditioning. Packet shows collision rate dropping for m>=3 perturbed actors (page 8) but that is an observation, not framed as a limitation.
